question: Which radioactive isotope has a half-life of 5770 years, which is commonly used to estimate the age of organic materials such as paper and parchment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Carbon-14 (14C) is a radioactive isotope of carbon with a half-life of about 5,730 years (commonly rounded to 5770 years in some references), used in radiocarbon dating. (कार्बन डेटिंग — 14C)

 

• It is widely used to determine the age of organic materials such as paper, parchment, wood, bones, and fossils by measuring the remaining proportion of 14C relative to stable 12C.

 

• Radiocarbon dating was developed by Willard Libby in the late 1940s, for which he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1960.

 

• 14C is continuously produced in the upper atmosphere by cosmic ray interactions with nitrogen and decays by beta emission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Carbon-12 (12C) is the most abundant, stable isotope of carbon and is the standard reference for atomic mass.

 

• Other isotopic dating methods include Uranium-lead dating (for rocks) and Potassium-argon dating (for very old geological samples).

 

NOTE

 

• 9C (Option 1): Not a naturally significant or commonly used isotope of carbon; it is an extremely short-lived, unstable isotope.

 

• 12C (Option 2): This is the stable, most abundant isotope of carbon and is not radioactive, so it cannot be used for radiometric dating.

 

• 17C (Option 4): Not a recognised isotope used in dating; carbon isotopes used practically are limited to 12C, 13C, and 14C.

question: Who said 'PURA is one of the mechanisms which will be utilised for transforming our villages into productive economic zones'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is APJ Abdul Kalam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, the 11th President of India, conceived the idea of PURA (Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) as a strategy for balanced rural development. (पुरा योजना — डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम)

 

• He described PURA as a mechanism for transforming villages into productive economic zones by providing them with physical, electronic, and knowledge connectivity along with urban-standard amenities, without causing rural-to-urban migration.

 

• The concept was first outlined by Kalam in his book "India 2020" and later promoted as a national scheme by the Government of India (launched as a pilot in 2004 and later as a modified scheme, PURA 2.0, in 2011-12).

 

• The core idea was to bridge the rural-urban divide by bringing four types of connectivity to villages: physical, electronic, knowledge, and economic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. Kalam is often called the "Missile Man of India" for his contribution to India's missile and space programmes, and served as President of India from 2002 to 2007.

 

• The PURA scheme was later restructured as a Ministry of Rural Development scheme aimed at cluster-based rural development.

 

NOTE

 

• Manmohan Singh (Option 2): Former Prime Minister of India, known for economic liberalisation reforms of 1991, not the originator of the PURA concept.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 3): Known for the "Drain of Wealth" theory and his book Poverty and Un-British Rule in India; he predates PURA by over a century.

 

• Atal Bihari Vajpayee (Option 4): Former Prime Minister of India who launched schemes like the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), but PURA was Kalam's idea.

question: Which of the following is the right relationship between geometric length (Lg) and magnetic length (Lm)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is **Lm = 5/6 * Lg**.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For a bar magnet, the magnetic length (Lm) is defined as the distance between its two magnetic poles, while the geometric length (Lg) is the actual physical length of the magnet. (चुंबकीय लंबाई — 5/6 गुना ज्यामितीय लंबाई)

 

• Since the magnetic poles are not located exactly at the physical ends of the bar magnet but slightly inside, the magnetic length is slightly less than the geometric length.

 

• The standard empirical relationship used in physics is Lm = (5/6) × Lg, i.e., the magnetic length is approximately 5/6th of the geometric length.

 

• This relation is used while calculating the magnetic moment of a bar magnet, given by M = m × Lm, where m is the pole strength.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ratio of magnetic length to geometric length for a bar magnet is a standard approximation used in NCERT-level physics (magnetism chapter).

 

• A magnetic dipole is characterised by its magnetic dipole moment, a vector quantity directed from the south pole to the north pole along the magnetic axis.

 

NOTE

 

• Lm = 6/5 × Lg (Option 1): Incorrect; this would make the magnetic length greater than the geometric length, which is physically inconsistent.

 

• Lm = Lg (Option 2): Incorrect; this assumes the poles lie exactly at the physical ends, which is not the accepted approximation.

 

• Lm = 2RY (Option 3): Incorrect; this is an unrelated/meaningless expression for this relationship.

question: Who was the first woman graduate of Calcutta University?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kadambini Ganguly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kadambini Ganguly (1861-1923) was one of the first two female graduates of the British Empire and the first woman graduate of the University of Calcutta, graduating in 1883. (कादंबिनी गांगुली — कलकत्ता विश्वविद्यालय की प्रथम स्नातक)

 

• She was also one of the first South Asian female physicians trained in Western medicine, qualifying from Calcutta Medical College in 1886.

 

• Chandramukhi Basu graduated in the same year (1883) as Kadambini Ganguly, but from Bethune College under Calcutta University's affiliation; Kadambini is specifically credited as the first to complete a full graduate degree.

 

• She was also an active participant in the Indian nationalist movement and social reform, and one of the earliest women to address the Indian National Congress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anandibai Joshi and Kadambini Ganguly are together regarded as pioneering Indian women doctors of the late 19th century.

 

• The University of Calcutta, established in 1857, was one of the first modern universities in India (along with Bombay and Madras Universities).

 

NOTE

 

• Sarojini Naidu (Option 1): Known as the "Nightingale of India"; she was a poet, freedom fighter, and the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (1925) and first woman Governor of an Indian state (UP).

 

• Annie Besant (Option 2): A British theosophist and social reformer who became President of the Indian National Congress in 1917; she was not an Indian graduate.

 

• Rajkumari Amritkaur (Option 4): India's first Health Minister; she was not the first woman graduate of Calcutta University.

question: Which of these statements is true?
option_1: At lower rates of interest, people will have a lower preference for liquidity.
option_2: At higher rates of interest transactions demand for money will be higher.
option_3: At lower rates of interest, speculative demand for money will be higher.
option_4: At higher rates of interest liquidity preference of people will increase
solution_text:
The correct answer is At lower rates of interest, speculative demand for money will be higher.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to J.M. Keynes' Liquidity Preference Theory, the demand for money has three motives: transactions, precautionary, and speculative. (तरलता वरीयता सिद्धांत — ब्याज दर और सट्टा मांग)

 

• The speculative demand for money arises because people prefer to hold cash rather than bonds when they expect interest rates to rise (and bond prices to fall) in the future.

 

• At lower rates of interest, the opportunity cost of holding money (i.e., the interest foregone) is low, and people expect rates to rise in the future, so they prefer to hold more cash (higher speculative demand) rather than invest in bonds.

 

• Conversely, at higher rates of interest, the opportunity cost of holding idle cash is high, so speculative demand for money falls as people prefer interest-bearing assets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The transactions demand for money depends primarily on the level of income, not the interest rate, and is relatively interest-inelastic.

 

• The liquidity preference (demand for money) curve slopes downward with respect to the interest rate — i.e., demand for money falls as interest rate rises.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect; at lower interest rates, people's preference for liquidity (holding cash) is actually higher, not lower.

 

• Option 2: Incorrect; transactions demand for money depends on income levels, not directly on the interest rate, and does not necessarily rise with higher interest rates.

 

• Option 4: Incorrect; at higher interest rates, the liquidity preference of people decreases (people prefer to invest rather than hold idle cash).

question: Which of the following is an example of capital receipt?
option_1: Disinvestment of Public Sector Banks by the Government
solution_text:
The correct answer is Disinvestment of Public Sector Banks by the Government.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A capital receipt either creates a liability or reduces the assets of the government; it does not arise from normal government operations. (पूंजीगत प्राप्तियां — विनिवेश)

 

• Disinvestment (sale of government's shareholding in Public Sector Undertakings/Banks) reduces the government's assets, and hence the proceeds are classified as a capital receipt.

 

• Other examples of capital receipts include market borrowings, loans from the public, recovery of loans, and proceeds from disinvestment.

 

• Capital receipts are recorded in the Capital Budget and are used mainly for creating capital assets or repaying loans.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Revenue receipts, on the other hand, are receipts that neither create a liability nor reduce an asset — these include tax revenue (income tax, GST) and non-tax revenue (fees, fines, dividends).

 

• Recent examples of disinvestment include the government's stake sale in companies like Air India (strategic disinvestment) and various PSU banks/insurers.

 

NOTE

 

• Passport Fees (Option 2): This is a non-tax revenue receipt, collected as a fee for a government service, not a capital receipt.

 

• Land Registration Fees (Option 3): This is also a non-tax revenue receipt collected by the government for registering property transactions.

 

• General donation (Option 4): Donations received by the government are treated as revenue receipts, as they do not create any liability or reduce assets.

question: A father was speaking about the rich cultural heritage of India to his young son and his teenager friends. The fundamental duty in which Article was the father promoting?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51A (f).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A of the Indian Constitution lists the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A(f))

 

• Article 51A(f) states that it is the duty of every citizen "to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture", which matches the father speaking to his son about India's cultural heritage.

 

• Fundamental Duties are contained in Part IVA of the Constitution and are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts), unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

• Originally, 10 fundamental duties were added in 1976; an 11th duty (relating to providing education to children aged 6-14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties in India are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Russia).

 

• The list of Fundamental Duties currently stands at 11, covering respect for the Constitution, National Flag and Anthem, protection of the environment, scientific temper, and more.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 51A(e) (Option 2): Duty "to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India" and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

 

• Article 51A(d) (Option 3): Duty "to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so".

 

• Article 51A(c) (Option 4): Duty "to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India".

question: Which of the following options best describes the objective of Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) Scheme, 2016?
option_1: To provide financial assistance to entrepreneurs
option_2: To provide free healthcare services to the unemployed
option_3: To provide employment opportunities for rural women
option_4: To encourage employers to create new jobs
solution_text:
The correct answer is To encourage employers to create new jobs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) was launched in 2016 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to incentivise employers for generating new employment. (प्रधानमंत्री रोजगार प्रोत्साहन योजना — रोजगार सृजन)

 

• Under the scheme, the Government of India pays the employer's full contribution towards EPF and EPS (12% of wages) for new employees earning up to a specified wage ceiling, for the first three years of employment.

 

• The scheme aims to incentivise employers to increase the employment base of workers in their establishments, thereby also incentivising employees to formalise their jobs.

 

• PMRPY is implemented in coordination with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMRPY was subsumed under Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (ABRY), launched in 2020 to boost employment in the post-COVID recovery period.

 

• Other similar labour welfare schemes include the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) schemes announced in subsequent Union Budgets.

 

NOTE

 

• To provide financial assistance to entrepreneurs (Option 1): This describes schemes like Startup India or MUDRA Yojana, not PMRPY.

 

• To provide free healthcare services to the unemployed (Option 2): This is unrelated to PMRPY; healthcare is covered under schemes like Ayushman Bharat.

 

• To provide employment opportunities for rural women (Option 3): This is not the specific objective of PMRPY, which targets formal-sector employment generation broadly, not specifically rural women.

question: Who among the following leaders received the 'Lifetime Achievement Award' during the 13th Sansad Ratna Awards?
solution_text:
The correct answer is TK Rangarajan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 13th Sansad Ratna Awards were conferred for outstanding parliamentary performance during 2023, organised by the Prime Point Foundation. (संसद रत्न पुरस्कार — टी.के. रंगराजन)

 

• Veteran CPI(M) leader T.K. Rangarajan, a former Rajya Sabha MP from Tamil Nadu, was conferred the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 13th Sansad Ratna Awards.

 

• The Sansad Ratna Awards recognise Members of Parliament for their contribution to legislative debates, questions raised, and private member's bills, based on data analysis of parliamentary proceedings.

 

• The awards were presented at a ceremony that also honoured several sitting MPs across parties for their performance in Parliament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Prime Point Foundation, founded by Dr. K. Srinivasan, has been conferring Sansad Ratna Awards annually since 2010 based on empirical data from PRS Legislative Research.

 

• The Lifetime Achievement Award recognises veteran parliamentarians for their sustained contribution over decades in Parliament.

 

NOTE

 

• Chandrababu Naidu (Option 1): Senior political leader and former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, not the recipient of this particular award in this edition.

 

• Kumar Mangalam (Option 2): Not the recipient of the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 13th Sansad Ratna Awards.

 

• Sumitra Mahajan (Option 3): Former Lok Sabha Speaker (2014-2019), not the recipient of this specific award in this edition.

question: The name of Ustad Vilayat Khan is associated with which of the following Indian musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Vilayat Khan (1928-2004) was a legendary Indian classical musician renowned as a master sitar player. (उस्ताद विलायत खान — सितार)

 

• He belonged to the Imdadkhani gharana (Etawah gharana) of sitar playing and was known for developing the "Gayaki Ang" style, which imitates vocal music on the sitar.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1968) and Padma Vibhushan (declined in 2000), and is considered one of the greatest sitar virtuosos of the 20th century.

 

• He performed extensively across the world and was a key figure in popularising the sitar internationally alongside Pandit Ravi Shankar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous sitar players include Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Shahid Parvez Khan (Vilayat Khan's nephew).

 

• Vilayat Khan's son, Ustad Shujaat Khan, has also carried forward the family's sitar tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• Santoor (Option 1): Associated with musicians like Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.

 

• Bansuri (Option 3): Associated with musicians like Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia.

 

• Tabla (Option 4): Associated with musicians like Ustad Zakir Hussain and Ustad Alla Rakha.

question: Which state government launched the crop insurance portal 'Mukhya Mantri Bagwani Bima Yojana' in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Haryana government launched the crop insurance portal for the "Mukhya Mantri Bagwani Bima Yojana" (MBBY) in 2022. (मुख्यमंत्री बागवानी बीमा योजना — हरियाणा)

 

• The scheme provides insurance cover to horticulture (fruit and vegetable) crops against losses due to natural calamities like frost, hailstorm, and unseasonal rain.

 

• It was launched by the Haryana Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare Minister to help horticulture farmers secure compensation for crop damage.

 

• The portal enables farmers growing notified horticultural crops to register and claim insurance benefits online.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Haryana also runs the "Meri Fasal Mera Byora" portal for crop registration and the Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana for price deficiency compensation to farmers.

 

• At the national level, crop insurance is primarily provided through the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), launched in 2016.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Runs its own agricultural schemes but did not launch the Mukhya Mantri Bagwani Bima Yojana.

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Not the state associated with this particular horticulture insurance portal.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Has its own farmer welfare schemes but is not the state that launched this specific scheme.

question: When did British Empire Games start?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1930.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The British Empire Games, the forerunner of today's Commonwealth Games, were first held in 1930 in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. (राष्ट्रमंडल खेल — पहला आयोजन 1930)

 

• The idea for the Games is credited to Melville Marks Robinson, who organised the inaugural edition with 11 countries and around 400 athletes participating.

 

• The Games were later renamed the British Empire and Commonwealth Games (1954), then the British Commonwealth Games (1970), and finally the Commonwealth Games (from 1978).

 

• They are held every four years, similar to the Olympic Games, featuring nations of the Commonwealth of Nations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 Commonwealth Games were held in Birmingham, England; the 2026 Commonwealth Games are scheduled to be held in Glasgow, Scotland.

 

• India made its Commonwealth Games debut in 1934 (the 2nd edition, held in London).

 

NOTE

 

• 1936 (Option 1): This is the year of the Berlin Summer Olympics, not the first British Empire Games.

 

• 1938 (Option 2): The 3rd edition of the British Empire Games was held in Sydney in 1938, not the first.

 

• 1934 (Option 4): The 2nd edition of the Games was held in London in 1934; India made its debut this year, but the Games themselves started in 1930.

question: ____________ is the income of the Government, Which arises out of the property left by the people without a legal heir.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Escheat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Escheat refers to the reversion of property to the State (Government) when a person dies without a legal heir or valid will (intestate), and there is no one else legally entitled to claim the property. (एस्चीट — वारिसहीन संपत्ति सरकार को हस्तांतरण)

 

• It is a legal doctrine under which such unclaimed or heirless property becomes an income source for the government.

 

• The term originates from feudal law, where a lord's land would revert to him if a tenant died without heirs.

 

• In India, provisions relating to escheat are recognised as a residual power of the State under property and succession laws.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Escheat is considered a form of non-tax revenue for the government, though it is rare compared to sources like fees and fines.

 

• The principle is based on the maxim that "no property can remain without an owner", so ownership defaults to the State in the absence of an heir.

 

NOTE

 

• Moot (Option 2): A term used in law referring to a hypothetical case for academic argument/debate; unrelated to inheritance or government income.

 

• Felony (Option 3): A term for a serious criminal offence, unrelated to unclaimed property.

 

• Lien (Option 4): A legal right to retain possession of property belonging to another until a debt owed is discharged; unrelated to escheat.

question: Which of the following Indian states is NOT covered by the Deccan Plateau?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Deccan Plateau is a large, triangular plateau in peninsular (southern) India, bounded by the Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, and the Satpura-Vindhya ranges to the north. (दक्कन का पठार — मध्य प्रदेश शामिल नहीं)

 

• The Deccan Plateau primarily covers states including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and parts of Tamil Nadu.

 

• Madhya Pradesh largely lies in the Central Highlands region (including the Malwa Plateau and Vindhya Range), which is geographically and geologically distinct from the Deccan Plateau, and hence is not considered part of it.

 

• The Deccan Plateau is famous for its black soil (regur soil), formed from Deccan Trap basaltic lava flows, ideal for cotton cultivation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Deccan Traps, one of the largest volcanic provinces in the world, were formed around 66 million years ago, coinciding with the end of the Cretaceous period.

 

• The Deccan Plateau slopes gently from west to east, which is why most peninsular rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Telangana (Option 1): Lies entirely within the Deccan Plateau region.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): A major part of the state lies on the Deccan Plateau, characterised by black soil.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): The Rayalaseema and interior regions of Andhra Pradesh lie on the Deccan Plateau.

question: Which hypothesis was proposed by Paul Ehrlich to suggest the importance of species richness in the maintenance of ecosystems?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rivet popper hypothesis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rivet Popper Hypothesis was proposed by ecologist Paul Ehrlich (along with Anne Ehrlich) to explain the importance of species richness in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem. (रिवेट पॉपर परिकल्पना — पॉल एर्लिच)

 

• The hypothesis compares an ecosystem to an airplane held together by rivets, where each species is like one rivet. Loss of a few rivets (species) may not immediately affect the plane's function, but as more rivets are removed, the plane (ecosystem) becomes dangerously weak and eventually fails.

 

• It emphasizes that every species contributes to the stability of the ecosystem, and even seemingly minor/redundant species should not be considered dispensable for conservation purposes.

 

• This hypothesis stands in contrast to the redundancy hypothesis, proposed by ecologist Brian Walker, which argues that most species are functionally redundant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Paul Ehrlich is also well known for his controversial book "The Population Bomb" (1968), which discussed the impacts of overpopulation.

 

• Species richness and species diversity are key components of biodiversity, extensively discussed in ecology under NCERT Biology (Class 12).

 

NOTE

 

• Portfolio hypothesis (Option 1): Suggests that a diverse "portfolio" of species buffers ecosystem function against environmental fluctuations, similar to a financial portfolio, but this is not the concept credited to Ehrlich here.

 

• Redundancy hypothesis (Option 2): Proposed by Brian Walker; argues most species are ecologically redundant and only a few "driver" species are critical.

 

• Predation hypothesis (Option 3): Relates to the role of predators in controlling species diversity (e.g., keystone predator concept), not the concept attributed to Ehrlich in this context.

question: Paika dance is performed in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Paika dance is a traditional martial folk dance of Jharkhand, performed mainly by the Munda and other tribal communities. (पाइका नृत्य — झारखंड)

 

• It is a war dance, performed by dancers dressed as warriors carrying swords and shields, depicting martial skills and valour, often accompanied by drums like the dhol and nagara.

 

• The dance is traditionally performed during festivals and special occasions to showcase martial traditions and cultural heritage of the tribal communities of the region.

 

• Jharkhand is home to numerous vibrant tribal dance forms, of which Paika is one of the most prominent martial dances.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important folk dances of Jharkhand include Jhumar, Chhau, Karma, Domkach, and Santhal dance.

 

• Jharkhand's Chhau dance is a UNESCO-recognised Intangible Cultural Heritage dance form, also performed as a masked martial dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Goa (Option 1): Known for dance forms like Fugdi, Dhalo, and Dekhni, not Paika.

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Known for Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, and Theyyam, not Paika.

 

• Assam (Option 3): Known for dance forms like Bihu and Sattriya, not Paika.

question: Maharshi Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj organisation in 1875 at which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maharshi Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay (now Mumbai) in 1875. (आर्य समाज — बॉम्बे, 1875)

 

• The Arya Samaj was a Hindu reform movement based on the infallibility of the Vedas, promoting the slogan "Back to the Vedas" and opposing idol worship, caste discrimination, and social evils like child marriage.

 

• Dayanand Saraswati authored the influential text "Satyarth Prakash" (The Light of Truth), which laid out the philosophical foundations of the Arya Samaj.

 

• The movement later established its headquarters/major centre of activity in Lahore, where it became especially influential in Punjab.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arya Samaj promoted institutions like the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) schools and colleges to spread modern education alongside Vedic values.

 

• Dayanand Saraswati's real name was Mool Shankar; he was born in Tankara, Gujarat, in 1824.

 

NOTE

 

• Lahore (Option 1): Became a major centre and later the headquarters of Arya Samaj's activities, but the organisation was founded in Bombay, not Lahore.

 

• Delhi (Option 2): Not the founding location of Arya Samaj.

 

• Amritsar (Option 3): Not the founding location of Arya Samaj.

question: Which of the following is a feature of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lengthiest written constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Constitution is the lengthiest written constitution in the world, originally containing 395 Articles in 22 Parts and 8 Schedules; it currently has about 470 Articles in 25 Parts and 12 Schedules after amendments. (भारत का संविधान — विश्व का सबसे लंबा लिखित संविधान)

 

• Its length is attributed to the vastness and diversity of India, borrowing extensively from other constitutions worldwide, and the detailed nature of provisions covering both the Union and the States.

 

• It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is regarded as the chief architect (Father) of the Indian Constitution as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Constitution is often described as a "blend of rigidity and flexibility", but it is predominantly considered flexible since most provisions can be amended by a simple parliamentary majority.

 

• India has single citizenship, unlike federations such as the USA which allow dual (state and national) citizenship.

 

NOTE

 

• Rigid constitution (Option 2): Incorrect; the Indian Constitution is largely flexible, with most provisions amendable by simple or special majority, not requiring extraordinary procedures like fully rigid constitutions (e.g., USA).

 

• Presidential form of government (Option 3): Incorrect; India follows a Parliamentary form of government, with the Council of Ministers responsible to the Lok Sabha, unlike the USA's presidential system.

 

• Dual citizenship (Option 4): Incorrect; India provides for single citizenship for all citizens, unlike federal countries like the USA.

question: Modhera dance festival is performed in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Modhera Dance Festival, also known as the Uttarardh Mahotsav, is held every year at the historic Sun Temple in Modhera, located in the Mehsana district of Gujarat. (मोढेरा नृत्य महोत्सव — गुजरात)

 

• The festival is typically held in January (around Makar Sankranti/Uttarayan) and showcases various classical Indian dance forms performed against the backdrop of the magnificent Sun Temple.

 

• The Sun Temple at Modhera was built in the 11th century by King Bhima I of the Solanki (Chaulukya) dynasty, dedicated to the Sun god (Surya).

 

• The festival is organised by the Gujarat Tourism Department to promote both the state's heritage architecture and its rich classical dance traditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sun Temple at Modhera is designed such that the first rays of the sun during equinoxes fall on the idol in the sanctum, showcasing ancient architectural precision.

 

• Gujarat also hosts other cultural festivals such as the Rann Utsav in the Kutch region and the Navratri Festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Known for the Ellora Dance and Music Festival, not Modhera.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Known for the Hampi Utsav and Pattadakal Dance Festival, not Modhera.

 

• Manipur (Option 4): Known for the Sangai Festival, not Modhera.

question: On which planet has a rotating oval of clouds, twice as wide as Earth, called the 'Great Red Spot' been observed for more than 300 years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jupiter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Great Red Spot is a giant, persistent anticyclonic storm on Jupiter, the largest planet in the solar system. (महान लाल धब्बा — बृहस्पति ग्रह)

 

• It is a rotating oval-shaped storm of high pressure that has been observed continuously for more than 300 years, with early telescopic observations dating back to the 17th century.

 

• The storm is roughly 1.3 times the diameter of Earth (historically described as up to twice Earth's width in earlier observations, though it has been shrinking over recent decades).

 

• Jupiter has a strong, banded atmosphere composed primarily of hydrogen and helium, with numerous storms and belts driven by its rapid rotation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system and has the most known moons, including the four large Galilean moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.

 

• NASA's Juno spacecraft, launched in 2011, has been studying Jupiter's atmosphere, including the Great Red Spot, since 2016.

 

NOTE

 

• Neptune (Option 1): Known for its own storm system, the "Great Dark Spot", observed by Voyager 2, not the Great Red Spot.

 

• Mercury (Option 2): The smallest planet, closest to the Sun, with virtually no atmosphere and no such storm feature.

 

• Venus (Option 4): Known for its thick, toxic atmosphere and extreme greenhouse effect, but not the Great Red Spot.

question: Padma Shri awardee of 2019 and classical dancer, Narthaki Nataraj belongs to which of the following dance genres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Narthaki Nataraj is a renowned transgender Bharatanatyam dancer from Tamil Nadu, known for reviving and preserving traditional dance forms. (नर्तकी नटराज — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2019, becoming the first transgender person to receive this honour in the field of art.

 

• She trained under legendary gurus and is known for her contributions to the Pandanallur style of Bharatanatyam, and also runs a dance school to train young artists.

 

• She has performed extensively in India and abroad, representing Indian classical dance on international platforms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu, traditionally performed in Hindu temples.

 

• Other notable Bharatanatyam exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale, Yamini Krishnamurthy, and Padma Subrahmanyam.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 1): Classical dance form from Odisha; notable exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Sonal Mansingh.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): Classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh; notable exponents include Raja and Radha Reddy.

 

• Sattriya (Option 4): Classical dance form from Assam, associated with the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) founded by Srimanta Sankardev.

question: Ibn Battuta, a traveller, hailed from which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Morocco.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ibn Battuta (1304-1369) was a famous Muslim traveller and scholar born in Tangier, Morocco. (इब्न बतूता — मोरक्को)

 

• He is renowned for his extensive travels across the medieval Islamic world and beyond, documented in his travelogue known as the "Rihla".

 

• He visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who appointed him as the Qazi (judge) of Delhi for several years.

 

• His travels covered over 75,000 miles across North Africa, the Middle East, South Asia, Central Asia, and China, making him one of history's greatest travellers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ibn Battuta's accounts are a valuable historical source for understanding the Delhi Sultanate, particularly the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

 

• Other notable foreign travellers to medieval India include Al-Biruni (from Khwarezm) and Marco Polo (from Venice, Italy).

 

NOTE

 

• Iran (Option 1): Ibn Battuta travelled through Iran (Persia) during his journeys, but he was not born there.

 

• Afghanistan (Option 2): He passed through this region en route to India, but it was not his native country.

 

• Mongolia (Option 4): Not associated with Ibn Battuta's origin; he did travel to parts of the Mongol-influenced regions of Central Asia and China.

question: Who among the following Indian wrestlers won the Gold Medal in the 57 kg category at the Asian Wrestling Championship 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aman Sherawat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aman Sehrawat won the gold medal in the men's freestyle 57 kg category at the Asian Wrestling Championships 2023, held in Astana, Kazakhstan. (आमन सहरावत — एशियाई कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप 2023)

 

• In the final, he defeated Japan's Rei Higuchi to claim the title, marking a significant achievement in his young career.

 

• This was his first senior-level gold medal at a major international wrestling event, establishing him as a top contender in the lightweight freestyle category.

 

• Aman Sehrawat went on to win a bronze medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics in the men's freestyle 57 kg category, becoming India's youngest individual Olympic medallist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Asian Wrestling Championships are organised annually by the United World Wrestling (UWW) Asia body, covering freestyle, Greco-Roman, and women's wrestling.

 

• India has historically produced strong wrestlers in this weight category, including Ravi Kumar Dahiya, an Olympic silver medallist (Tokyo 2020) in the same 57 kg category.

 

NOTE

 

• Anirudh Galia (Option 1): Not the gold medallist in the 57 kg category at this event.

 

• Deepak Mirka (Option 2): Not the gold medallist in the 57 kg category at this event.

 

• Neeraj Chhikra (Option 3): Not the gold medallist in the 57 kg category at this event.

question: ________ became the first Indian footballer to play in the UEFA Women's Champions League in 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manisha Kalyan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manisha Kalyan, an Indian women's football forward from Punjab, became the first Indian footballer (male or female) to play in the UEFA Women's Champions League in 2022. (मनीषा कल्याण — यूईएफए महिला चैंपियंस लीग)

 

• She achieved this milestone after signing with Apollon Ladies FC, a Cyprus-based football club, in August 2022.

 

• She is a member of the Indian women's national football team and had earlier played for clubs in the Indian Women's League.

 

• This achievement was widely celebrated as a historic first for Indian football at the club level in European competitions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The UEFA Women's Champions League is the premier European club competition for women's football, similar to the men's UEFA Champions League.

 

• Manisha Kalyan later moved to other European clubs, continuing to represent Indian football on the international club stage.

 

NOTE

 

• Pyari Xaxa (Option 1): A notable Indian women's footballer, but not the one who achieved this specific UEFA Champions League milestone.

 

• Ashalata Devi (Option 2): Captain of the Indian women's national football team, but not the first to play in the UEFA Women's Champions League.

 

• Jyoti Chouhan (Option 4): Not associated with this particular UEFA Women's Champions League milestone.

question: The committee headed by Radhakrishna recommended ________.
option_1: The initiation of Regulatory Policy for Microfinance Institutions
option_3: the initiation of the National Rural Livelihood Mission
solution_text:
The correct answer is the initiation of the National Rural Livelihood Mission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Radhakrishna Committee (Committee on Financial Inclusion / Agricultural Indebtedness, headed by Dr. R. Radhakrishna) submitted its report in 2007, examining issues of rural credit and poverty alleviation programmes. (राधाकृष्ण समिति — राष्ट्रीय ग्रामीण आजीविका मिशन)

 

• Based on the committee's recommendations for restructuring rural self-employment programmes, the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was restructured into the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM), launched in 2011.

 

• NRLM (later renamed DAY-NRLM, or Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihood Mission, in 2015) aims to reduce rural poverty by promoting self-employment and organisation of rural poor into Self-Help Groups (SHGs).

 

• The committee's recommendations emphasised a demand-driven, community-based approach to rural livelihoods, which shaped the design of NRLM.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NRLM is one of the world's largest poverty alleviation programmes, implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.

 

• NRLM has a sister urban programme called the National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM), launched in 2013.

 

NOTE

 

• The initiation of Regulatory Policy for Microfinance Institutions (Option 1): This relates to recommendations of other committees like the Malegam Committee (2011) on microfinance regulation.

 

• The creation of Project EShakti (Option 2): Project E-Shakti was an RBI initiative for digitising Self-Help Group data, unrelated to the Radhakrishna Committee.

 

• The creation of RRBs (Option 4): Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were created in 1975 based on the recommendations of the Narasimham Working Group, not the Radhakrishna Committee.
